pr_title: feat: Add support for product imports

comments.body: The downloadable template is delimited with semicolons (`Product Id;Product Handle;...`). The backend parses the upload with `convertCsvToJson` (packages/core/utils/src/csv/csvtojson.ts:9), which calls `csv2json` with no `delimiter` option, so it expects commas. A user who downloads this template, fills it in and uploads it gets one giant header named `Product Id;Product Handle;...`. `product["Product Handle"]` is then undefined, and `parseProductCsvStep` (packages/core/core-flows/src/product/steps/parse-product-csv.ts:12) throws "Product handle is required when importing products". The template fails the import it is meant to demonstrate. The header and all rows need to be comma-separated.

The old `NotificationFile` showed `file?.filename ?? file.url`. The new code passes `filename={data.file.filename ?? ""}` to `FilePreview`, which renders only `{filename}`. When a notification has a `file.url` but no `filename`, the row now shows empty text. The download anchor gets `download=""` instead of the `Date.now()` fallback, because `"" ?? ...` never falls through. This is a regression from the previous fallback to the URL.

The CSV import uploader reuses the image-upload strings `products.media.uploadImagesLabel` and `products.media.uploadImagesHint`. The dropzone will say "upload images" while asking for a CSV file. The change also adds `products.import.*` translation keys, but none of them is used here.
